what: Las Vegas Sands owns and operates casino resorts in Macao and Singapore. It no longer operates in Las Vegas despite the name. Marina Bay Sands in Singapore is its single most profitable property.
customers: Chinese, other Asian and international visitors gambling, staying and attending conventions at its resorts.
money: The Venetian Macao, Londoner, Parisian and Plaza
moat: Casino licences in two of the only places in Asia where large-scale gambling is legal, with properties that cost billions to build and cannot be replicated.
risks: It depends entirely on Chinese and Asian visitation, which Chinese policy can affect
Macao licence conditions require continued investment
Renovation work disrupts revenue at individual properties
opportunities: Revenue grew about 15% last year and about 47% a year over three years as Asian travel recovered
The Marina Bay Sands expansion adds capacity in a market with only two licences
A dividend yield around 3% with large buybacks
watch: Macao gross gaming revenue and Marina Bay Sands profitability.
